runners_data.name: Thats My Boy Luke
runners_data.note: Stall 1 is his greatest asset here — Tim Easterby's gelding tracks prominently and the low draw gives him an effortless passage to a ground-saving position behind Our Nicola; eight runs on Good ground show consistent place efforts without a win but the Strand Scorecard marks him as the highest-confidence selection and the tactical setup suits him perfectly.

runners_data.name: Book Of Life
runners_data.note: Patrick Morris's six-year-old has a tidy recent record including two wins on Standtrack and one Good-ground placed effort at 8f, and from stall 7 he will need to find his rhythm quickly to sit in a useful midfield position; his 1/15 sim-going strike rate on true Good is a mild concern, but his form figures are competitive at this level.

runners_data.name: King Sharja
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's veteran has placed at 7f and 8f on this track before and travels in midfield, though a 0W1P record on Good turf in the last five runs and a middling draw in stall 5 means he will need a strong sectional finish to get involved; his recent form figures — 240562 — hint at a horse that finds ways to be placed without converting.

runners_data.name: Our Nicola
runners_data.note: The race's only front-runner, David & Nicola Barron's four-year-old will push forward from stall 9 to lead, but the widest draw on a left-favouring track is a genuine logistical obstacle to establishing that position cleanly; she has placed at 7f on Soft and Standard but her OR of 44 is the lowest in the field, meaning she will need to translate her lead into something the others cannot peg back.

runners_data.name: Approaching Dawn
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's Amie Waugh-ridden hold-up performer has two wins and three places from 14 runs on similar Good going, which is the strongest sim-going record in this field, and her one win came at 8f on Good ground; the Strand Scorecard flags her as the chief danger and that assessment is supported by the data, though from stall 6 she will need a clean passage through midfield.

runners_data.name: Hale Bopp
runners_data.note: Daragh Bourke's eight-year-old has placed at 8f on Good twice in the last five runs and races from the hold-up position, giving him an obvious profile for the closing stages, but his overall record — 0W2P — on this going and a trainer operating off a low base (0/3 in 14 days) suggests he is more likely a place contender than a winner.

runners_data.name: Due Respect
runners_data.note: Caitlin Bissett's four-year-old carries a clear finishing concern flagged in the data, prone to fading late, and despite a prominent running style he is unlikely to see out a strongly-run mile in the final furlong; visored, with 0 wins and 0 places from 10 recent sim-going efforts, this is a horse to treat as a potential pace-influencer rather than a serious winning candidate.

runners_data.name: Eagles Dream
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's four-year-old holds up and has placed once in three runs on Good ground, but a form string of 5-8805 over distances beyond today's trip suggests this mile may be sharper than he prefers; from low stall 2 Lexie Clarkson (7lb claimer) faces the challenge of timing a late run from a horse with limited finishing punch.

runners_data.name: Defence Missile
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's four-year-old has a strong recent mark — winning last time at 8f on Standard — and races prominently from stall 3, giving him the profile to hold a useful position early; however a 0W0P record on Good turf across three attempts, combined with pinhooker headgear, means he must overcome a surface question to translate his all-weather form here.

races.paceDynamic: Our Nicola is the sole confirmed front-runner and, drawn widest in stall 9 on a course where low draws are favoured, will need to cross smartly to secure the rail and dictate from the front — if she gets there uncontested, she sets a single, sustainable gallop on Good ground that is unlikely to be pressured by any of the prominent trio (Thats My Boy Luke, Defence Missile, Due Respect). Thats My Boy Luke from stall 1 holds the prime low draw and will slot in just behind Our Nicola at minimal cost, giving him a perfect stalking position as the race settles into a rhythm. The hold-up horses — Approaching Dawn, Hale Bopp, Eagles Dream — will face a conventional closing challenge against a pace that is genuine but not frantic, meaning they need a strong, sustained finish rather than a sprint. This shape, a controlled single pace-setter with a well-placed prominent stalker from stall 1, heavily favours the prominent-to-mid profile that can travel in the slipstream and pick off a tiring leader in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stalker Picks Off Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Our Nicola sets her customary honest front-running pace and the prominent horses track comfortably without being stretched.
scenarios.body: Our Nicola's solo lead produces a fair but manageable gallop, leaving the horse in the prime stalking slot with energy in reserve to quicken past the dying leader in the final furlong; Thats My Boy Luke from stall 1 is ideally placed to exploit this and Book Of Life, with strong Good-ground form, can mount a challenge from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Launches Late
scenarios.trigger: If Our Nicola's pace is stronger than expected or the field bunches, allowing the hold-up horses a run at the leaders in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A genuine end-to-end gallop stretches the race sufficiently that the hold-up brigade get a target to aim at, with Approaching Dawn the most likely beneficiary given two wins at 8f on Good and a proven ability to pick up from the rear at this course configuration; Hale Bopp has placed twice on identical Good ground and can follow Approaching Dawn's lead if the pace collapses in front of them.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Contested Early Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Defence Missile or Due Respect push forward aggressively and compete with Our Nicola for the lead, lifting the tempo beyond a sustainable level.
scenarios.body: A hot early pace drains the leaders and prominent horses, opening the door for those who hold up to arrive with the most petrol in the tank in the closing stages; Approaching Dawn is the obvious beneficiary here with her strong late-running profile, while Eagles Dream at a longer price could pick up the pieces if the pace truly collapses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Leader Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Our Nicola is completely untroubled in front and the pace is so dawdling that no closer can generate sufficient momentum to get to her.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race at a crawl can enable a lone leader to simply outstay a field that has spent its energy fighting for position rather than running; Our Nicola would be the direct beneficiary, though this scenario is unlikely given her low OR and the competitive nature of the field snapping at her heels.

watchPoints.text: Watch Our Nicola crossing from stall 9 to the rail at the break — if she is checked or impeded before establishing the lead, the race loses its only pace-setter and the shape becomes unpredictable for the entire field.

Approaching Dawn's ability to find a clean run through the field between the half-mile and two-furlong marks is critical — if she gets boxed in during the mid-race, her strong late kick may arrive too late on this tight track.

Due Respect is flagged as a front-runner prone to fading; if he pushes forward alongside Our Nicola from stall 8, he risks igniting a contested early pace that would compromise both his own chance and the race shape for prominent horses.

Thats My Boy Luke's form at 8f on Good shows consistent placed efforts (4th, 5th, 6th, 3rd in last four) but no win — watch whether Jake Dickson can make the most of the low draw to time his run, or whether this horse's tendency to be outpointed at the finish recurs.

Eagles Dream and Hale Bopp both hold up from low draws (2 and 4) — if the early pace is moderate, these two may find themselves tracking closer than intended, effectively racing out of role and crowding the stalking positions occupied by Thats My Boy Luke and Defence Missile.

runners_data.name: Royal Strike
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer for Karl Burke, finished 2nd at 5f on soft and has placed at this level before; Good ground suits per sim-going record (1 place from 3 runs) and the 10-day turnaround is fine, but drawn 2 could trap it on the inner in the early prominent scramble|

runners_data.name: Desert Smoke
runners_data.note: Only genuine hold-up type in the race, trained by Hugo Palmer with a modest T14 strike rate; three consecutive declining finishes at 6f on Good and soft suggest no strong form momentum, and stepping back to 5f with a hold-up style in a fast-run race is a tough ask|

runners_data.name: Star People
runners_data.note: Jason Hart partners a horse with an admirable placed record — four runner-up or third finishes from six starts — on Good ground at 5f and 6f; consistent but unable to win from the prominent position, and draw 7 is manageable, though the prominent congestion 2-3 out is a real risk for a horse who needs a clean run|

runners_data.name: Inca Warrior
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's gelding is by nature a prominent racer but is placed in midfield here because this pace-heavy field gives him no realistic chance of securing his preferred position; drawn 1, he could push forward but faces three dedicated front-runners making that path difficult, and three consecutive 4th-5th finishes at 5f on Good reduce confidence even if he does find a clear passage|

runners_data.name: Needin' U
runners_data.note: Won last time at 5f on Good — the precise conditions repeating today — and the Michael & David Easterby operation is in strong form with four winners from 36 runs in 14 days; Billy Garritty's booking is positive and the headgear (hood) has been worn in wins before; draw 9 is wide but on a flat track with no turn, this is manageable and the prominent style suits this race shape directly|

runners_data.name: Fern Clyde
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's filly has a winning strike on Good ground at 6f and has placed six times from seven attempts in similar conditions, suggesting class and consistency; the 40-day absence and headgear combination (hood and tongue-tie) bear watching, but this is a trainer who has 16 winners in 14 days and the drop to 5f from recent 6f efforts could sharpen her up|

runners_data.name: Lexington Boom
runners_data.note: Clear front-runner with strong Musselburgh-style form: won at 5f Good, placed twice at the same trip and going; this is his natural race shape and draw 3 gives him the clearest path to the lead; the key question is whether Bellatina and Moonlight Tango allow him to control fractions or whether a battle develops|

runners_data.name: Bellatina
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's filly broke her maiden at 5f on Standard and has placed twice at this trip on Good; drawn 8 is wide for a front-runner wanting to establish early, and with Lexington Boom drawn on her inside, she may be forced to work hard for the lead rather than dictate — that energy cost matters over five furlongs|

runners_data.name: Moonlight Tango
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's runner won at 5f on Soft but has been out of form since, finishing 6th, 8th and 18th in recent starts on Good, which is a significant concern; a 43-day absence compounds the worry, and although she has front-running speed, her recent going figures on Good (sim-going: 0W from 3) make her the least reliable of the three confirmed pace-setters|

races.paceDynamic: Bellatina, Lexington Boom, and Moonlight Tango are all confirmed front-runners, and with three horses wanting to lead over five furlongs at Musselburgh, an honest-to-hard early gallop is virtually guaranteed — this is not a race where the pace will be manufactured, it is already baked in. The early scramble for supremacy will compress the field quickly, and any horse prominent but not leading will face a wall of competitors 2-3 furlongs out as Royal Strike, Star People, Fern Clyde, and Needin' U all compete for the limited space just behind the pace — traffic and interference are a real risk at that crucial junction. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel comfortably just off a fast pace and produce a sustained, gritty finish rather than a single explosive burst, meaning consistent prominent types with proven good-ground form at five furlongs hold the clearest structural advantage. This field carries more prominent/front-running types than the race can physically accommodate: of those mapping to the fore, Lexington Boom and Bellatina are best-placed to actually control the lead given draw and style, while Inca Warrior — a natural prominent racer — is unlikely to secure that position given the congestion and is mapped to midfield as a consequence.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three leaders burn each other off and a well-placed prominent type swoops past the weakening pace-setters in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The fierce early duel between Bellatina, Lexington Boom, and Moonlight Tango sets up a true-run race where the horse sitting just off the pace in a handy position reaps the reward as the leaders tie up; Good ground at Musselburgh on a flat five furlongs amplifies stamina late and punishes those who overcook it early

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners breaks cleanest, establishes a clear lead within the first furlong, and the others are forced to concede ground early
scenarios.body: With rivals checking or steering around the early chaos, a single leader controls fractions and never faces a sustained challenge until the line; Lexington Boom's recent course-and-distance form (1-2-2 on Good at 5f) gives that profile the most credible chance here

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closer Arrives
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way early battle is genuinely brutal and all leaders capitulate, allowing a hold-up horse to pick through the wreckage late
scenarios.body: Desert Smoke is the only true hold-up type in the field, but its form at 6f in Good has been modest and it has yet to show the required acceleration on this type of surface; a pace collapse scenario is plausible structurally but the profiling of the likely closers is weak, limiting conviction

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Traffic Chaos Decides
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent-congestion problem 2-3 furlongs out causes serious interference and the race is effectively decided by which runner navigates cleanest
scenarios.body: A field where four horses all want the same patch of ground creates a lottery element, and a horse who threads through late or benefits from a gap could win despite moderate form; Inca Warrior's redistribution to midfield means it races out of its natural role, undermining its chance in this shape

watchPoints.text: Watch the first two furlongs closely as Bellatina (draw 8), Lexington Boom (draw 3), and Moonlight Tango (draw 5) all break — whichever establishes a clear lead by the first furlong will dictate whether this becomes a controlled or a truly brutal race|

Needin' U drawn widest (stall 9) must navigate into a prominent position quickly; if the early scramble forces Billy Garritty to check or switch, the Strand Scorecard's top selection loses its core tactical advantage in the decisive 2-3 furlong zone|

The prominent congestion around 2-3 furlongs out involving Royal Strike, Star People, Fern Clyde, and Needin' U in a compressed group is the single biggest traffic risk of the race — any horse caught in a pocket or forced wide at that stage is likely done|

Moonlight Tango's recent Good-ground form is poor (0 wins or places from 3 runs in sim-going) and a 43-day break adds uncertainty; if she fades rapidly after setting pace, she could cause interference for horses tracking immediately behind|

Fern Clyde's 40-day absence and hood/tongue-tie combination suggest Tim Easterby has freshened her for this specific assignment — monitor her behaviour in the paddock and at the start as an indicator of how well she has returned|

races.paceDynamic: Bee Farmer (draw 4) and Showcasing Star (draw 10) are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from the off, creating a genuine, honest gallop over this 1m1f trip on good ground at Musselburgh. With two horses pushing each other through the early stages, the pace is unlikely to be dawdled, which should set up a true test of stamina and finishing quality rather than a sprint finish off a false gallop. This contested lead dynamic typically suits prominent-to-midfield horses who can travel close to the pace without burning energy fighting for position — horses like Minaun View, who can sit just off the pace and pounce, are the profile to be on. The field contains more hold-up types (Yermanthere, Motawaared, Mayor Of Maghera, Sunriseontheboyne) than the pace map can accommodate at the rear, meaning Motawaared in particular — a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map — is unlikely to secure its natural position and its chance must be discounted accordingly; Yermanthere and Mayor Of Maghera are the most likely to get a genuine closing position from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Bee Farmer and Showcasing Star ensure a genuine gallop and a prominent-travelling horse picks them off in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off ensuring the race is truly run, and a horse like Minaun View, who has the form, the going preference and a prominent style, can sit close enough to the pace to take full advantage when the leaders tie up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go hard enough to set up a strong finish for genuine hold-up horses staying on powerfully late.
scenarios.body: A truly honest early gallop sees the leaders weaken significantly inside the final furlong, opening the door for Yermanthere, who has proven course-and-distance winning form and relishes good ground, to close from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: One Front Runner Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Showcasing Star or Bee Farmer gains a clear early lead and the other drops away, allowing the leader to dictate a less pressured tempo.
scenarios.body: With the early battle neutralised and a single horse able to control the fractions, the lead converts into a winning position as there is not enough sustained pressure to burn them off, and Bee Farmer's higher recent form figures make them the more likely beneficiary if this shape materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or there is significant interference mid-race scrambling the field order.
scenarios.body: An untidy race with positional changes mid-race unsettles the prominent and hold-up runners alike, creating an unusual finish where a midfield type with fresh legs benefits from the chaos rather than the dominant pace narrative.

watchPoints.text: Minaun View's excellent sim-going record (11/15 on good, 3 wins) combined with a prominent style gives it a clear advantage if the contested early pace from Bee Farmer and Showcasing Star sets up a true-run race — watch for Cian Horgan to sit just off the leaders.

Yermanthere's hold-up profile is proven on good ground (1W 3P from 11 tries) and its recent 10f winning form makes it the most credible closer if the front-runners do burn each other off — Jake Dickson's 5lb claim makes it attractively weighted.

Showcasing Star's wide draw in stall 10 creates a tactical problem — if it has to push hard from wide to secure the lead against Bee Farmer, it may use up energy too early and capitulate sooner than anticipated, compromising the front-running scenario.

Motawaared is a genuine hold-up horse unlikely to get its preferred position in a field loaded with similar types — if it is pushed forward out of role, discount its chance; its best efforts have come from a settled rear position that will be difficult to find here.

Style Of Life carries the joint-top weight of 142lbs alongside Callianassa — watch whether the big weight blunts its finishing effort in the final stages, as OR 75 in a selling handicap over 1m1f on good ground is a stiff assignment for a horse with limited recent action.

races.name: Peterhead Fish Market Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Black Storm
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 7f/good combination most recently and has hit the frame in three of five starts on similar ground — a natural prominent racer whose 26-day freshness and Jason Hart booking for the in-form Katie Scott yard make this a serious player if the strong pace gifts a clear run from second position.

runners_data.name: Masaban
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's T14 strike rate of 4/31 is solid and Sam James is a reliable partner; this 3yo has a win and multiple placings on good ground and his front-running style means he will be at the centre of the early pace battle — how he handles the pressure from Carolus Magnus is the key question.

runners_data.name: Elizabetty
runners_data.note: Pierre-Louis Jamin picks up this Brian Ellison 3yo after a significant 162-day layoff, and a flagged tendency to fade in the finish is a genuine concern over 7f in a strong-gallop race; her sole win came at 7f on standard and she must prove fitness before punters lean on her.

runners_data.name: Carolus Magnus
runners_data.note: Billy Garritty partners this 8yo for Michael & David Easterby, who have posted a T14 of 4/36; Carolus Magnus won over 7f on good recently and has placed twice on similar going in the last five starts, making his front-running profile on flat Musselburgh turf the ideal shape — his draw in stall 7 means he must assert smartly to avoid being outpaced by Masaban from stall 4.

runners_data.name: Vince Le Prince
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 6yo has placed nine times on good ground in 14 attempts without winning — a chronic placer whose tongue-tie and 18-day turnaround are noted, but the inability to convert prominent runs into victories is a persistent concern over this trip.

runners_data.name: Pickersgill
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 4yo arrives on a quick 10-day turnaround with a hood, and while he placed at 6f on good in recent form, his five-run history is dominated by 6f and 5f starts on softer or standard surfaces — stepping up to 7f good is an unknown, and the wide draw in stall 10 compounds the positional challenge.

runners_data.name: Jesmond Dawn
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's 5yo has a genuine midfield running style and a recent 7-day break; placed in the field as a hold-up runner only because natural rear-of-field types are scarce, this horse typically races from the middle of the pack rather than dropping out, which structurally weakens any scenario requiring it to produce a deep late run.

runners_data.name: Monhammer
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's 8yo is the field's most authentic hold-up performer, boasting two course-and-distance wins on good ground from the rear — the 18-day break and apprentice claim (Ethan Tindall, 5lb) introduce execution risk, but the profile is genuine if the strong pace produces a tiring front rank.

runners_data.name: Keep Me Stable
runners_data.note: The second of Linda Perratt's pair, this 6yo has front-running style but draws in stall 1 — the widest starting point for a leader heading right-handed at Musselburgh — and with Masaban and Carolus Magnus drawn more centrally, securing the lead will require an aggressive and possibly costly burst; his recent 7f/good record (3rd, 2nd) shows ability but the positional disadvantage is real.

runners_data.name: Coconut Bay
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's 7yo has T14 of 4/12 suggesting yard form, but with an OR of just 53 and a form string including three finishes of 9th and 7th on good ground, Coconut Bay's ability to compete up front with higher-rated rivals in a strong-gallop race looks limited despite the leading style.

races.paceDynamic: Four horses — Masaban, Carolus Magnus, Keep Me Stable, and Coconut Bay — all want to lead, guaranteeing a strong early gallop over this flat Musselburgh 7f on good ground, with prominent riders Black Storm, Elizabetty, and Vince Le Prince immediately behind them creating serious congestion in the first two furlongs. Carolus Magnus and Masaban are the likeliest to actually secure the front rank given class and recent form; Keep Me Stable (drawn widest of the leaders at stall 1, facing a positional battle) and Coconut Bay (low OR of 53, sluggish recent record) are more likely to be crowded out or forced to settle. The field also contains Jesmond Dawn, a genuine midfield type redistributed to the rear only because hold-up runners are scarce — that horse is not a natural backmarker and its chance in a truly-come-from-behind shape is structurally compromised. A strong, sustained gallop over 7f on flat, good turf strongly favours a horse that can press or track the pace from a handy position and still find extra in the final 2f — the prominent-to-front-running profile that can handle the early battle and quicken when the fractions bite home.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Carolus Magnus and Masaban clear the early scrimmage and force a genuine pace duel, settling into the lead with Keep Me Stable applying pressure, the race becomes a test of who has the most left at the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: Carolus Magnus, with his proven Musselburgh win over this exact trip and course in recent form, is ideally suited to front-running on flat, good turf, and Billy Garritty's experience here gives him an edge over a pace-pressed field; Masaban, who handles good ground with a win at 8f suggesting stamina is not an issue, is the most dangerous rival in this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early duel between the four pace-seekers produces a genuinely hot gallop that ties itself in knots from the 3f pole, a well-positioned prominent horse sitting just off the pace is gifted a clear run.
scenarios.body: Black Storm, who has proven form at 7f on good ground with a recent win and multiple placed efforts at this trip and distance, is ideally placed in style and course suitability to sweep past a tiring front rank; Vince Le Prince has the prominent profile and a fine record on good ground but lacks a win in 14 similar-ground starts, making him the less reliable beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Appears
scenarios.trigger: If pace is ferocious enough to produce a carnage-style finish with the front rank stopping sharply inside the final furlong, a horse coming from off the pace could steal a placing.
scenarios.body: Monhammer, a genuine hold-up type with two wins over 7f on good at this very course and solid recent form showing a win and a sixth, has the profile to emerge from the rear if the race truly falls apart up front; however, an 18-day break and a 5lb claimer (Ethan Tindall) adds execution risk to an already-uncertain scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling between the four front-runners causes interference and the pace fails to develop cleanly, the race becomes a falsely-run sprint over the final 2f favouring sharp accelerators.
scenarios.body: Elizabetty, despite a lengthy 162-day absence and a concerning tendency to fade in finishes, has a win at 7f on good and could be dangerous in a sprint-to-the-line if traffic problems eliminate the usual stamina advantage; Pickersgill, with a draw in stall 10 and limited 7f course form, is an outsider in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Carolus Magnus and Masaban are both confirmed front-runners drawn in stalls 7 and 4 respectively — watch the first furlong for a genuine duel that could burn out one or both leaders before the 3f pole.

Keep Me Stable (stall 1) faces the hardest positional task of any front-runner: a wide starting gate heading right-handed at Musselburgh means early scrimmaging is likely, and any stumble or interference could cause knock-on trouble for prominent runners Black Storm and Elizabetty immediately behind.

Elizabetty's 162-day absence combined with the flagged fade-in-finish tendency means trainer Brian Ellison needs this one to bounce out fresh — a prominent-but-tiring effort from stall 3 could create a physical obstruction for runners trying to pass on the rail at the 2f marker.

Monhammer's hold-up profile is authentic, but Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim is its first meaningful test in a competitive handicap — if Tindall delays the challenge even slightly, the gap between the stopping leaders and the chasing group could be swallowed by the prominent types before Monhammer gets to them.

Jesmond Dawn's 7-day turnaround after a 6th at 7f/standard is tight, and its redistribution to the rear of this field belies a naturally mid-division style — if the race breaks slowly or produces a false pace in the first 2f, Dawn may end up further forward than expected, removing any hold-up advantage entirely.

races.name: Scots Association Musselburgh Gold Cup Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Wahraan
runners_data.note: Holds up from the rear and needs a truly searching gallop to get into contention; won over 18f on good ground 41 days ago and his sim-going record of 4/11 shows limited strike-rate, while the flat Musselburgh track offers no sharp bend to aid a sweeping late run.

runners_data.name: Fast Fred
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has finished second in five of his last ten on similar going; trainer Phillip Makin has had one winner from nine in the last 14 days but the horse's own recent form (six runs, five places) is compelling and he is ideally drawn to track the pace from stall one.

runners_data.name: Sax Appeal
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will have Dino Bellagio challenging him immediately; carries the joint-top weight of 142lbs and has not won in 15 sim-going starts, though three consecutive thirds suggest durability under pressure; Charlie Johnston's yard is in flying form (2/34 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Boxing Great
runners_data.note: Midfield runner with back-to-back wins on good ground over 18f and 15f — the form is there, but he needs the pace to be hot enough to bring his late effort into play; only 8 days since last run which is sharp, and trainer Karl Thornton has one winner from three in the 14-day window.

runners_data.name: Trojan Sun
runners_data.note: Prominent racer and the Strand Scorecard selection at medium confidence; Jim Goldie's yard is active (3/26 in 14 days) and apprentice Amie Waugh claims 3lb to offset a light OR of 72; a 6-day turnaround is sharp but the horse has a good-ground record of 2W5P from 15 applicable starts, and the prominent style suits this shape.

runners_data.name: Simple Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who drops sharply in class (OR 62) and has the lightest weight in the field at 123lbs; recent form shows a step back up in trip from 9f to 2m2f is needed, and his sim-going record of 8/9 with one minor placing offers little confidence — mainly a non-threatening outsider.

runners_data.name: Dino Bellagio
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will contest the early lead with Sax Appeal; his best recent form came over shorter (14f) on good and standard, and his only good-ground sim-going placing is 1/6 — if the duel with Sax Appeal costs him, he may weaken before the home turn rather than sustain.

races.paceDynamic: Sax Appeal and Dino Bellagio are both confirmed front-runners, meaning neither will yield willingly, and over 2m2f on good ground at Musselburgh they will set a genuine, honest gallop from the outset. The sustained pressure between the two pace-setters will stretch the field early and thin the margins at the business end, meaning the race will likely be run at a rhythm that suits horses who can travel prominently without burning matches. Fast Fred, a prominent racer with five placings from ten on similar ground, is ideally placed to track the pace from second or third, while Trojan Sun, also a prominent type with a strong good-ground record (10/15 runs), can cover ground off the leaders without overcommitting. This contested, honest gallop at a flat, fair track on good turf most clearly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the speed and produce a sustained late effort — hold-up horses like Wahraan and Simple Star face the additional task of making up ground on a track that does not provide the sharp finishing bend that typically plays into their hands.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Types Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Sax Appeal and Dino Bellagio fight for the lead and set a true gallop that stretches the hold-up horses and leaves closers with too much to do.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners trade blows throughout, setting a metronomic pace that drains the field, and horses positioned just behind the leaders are best placed to pounce from the home turn. Fast Fred and Trojan Sun, both natural prominent racers with solid good-ground credentials over staying trips, are ideally suited to capitalise on this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Breaks Clear Early
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners dominates and the other capitulates, leaving a single horse to dictate a solo lead at a controlled tempo.
scenarios.body: Sax Appeal or Dino Bellagio establishes unchallenged control, regulates the fractions, and conserves enough energy to repel challengers late. Sax Appeal, with a higher OR of 84 and three consecutive thirds, is better placed to sustain a solo lead if Dino Bellagio weakens first.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so fierce that the front-runners and prominent racers are exhausted, leaving ground-closers to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Wahraan and Boxing Great, both hold-up or midfield types, would benefit from a truly scorching early duel that leaves the prominent horses spent rounding the final turn. Boxing Great has back-to-back wins on good ground and brings strong recent form, giving him realistic claims if the pace truly capitulates ahead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Moderate Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners are checked or ease up under pressure and the race devolves into a falsely-run affair with a slow early tempo.
scenarios.body: A false pace would compress the field and turn the race into a sprint from home, favouring horses with a sharp late turn of foot rather than pure stamina. Simple Star and Wahraan lack the consistent finishing kick on good ground to be confident winners here, making this the least productive scenario for the field overall.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Sax Appeal or Dino Bellagio establishes dominance at the start — if one breaks smartly and the other is slow away, the pace duel may never truly materialise and the whole race shape changes.

Fast Fred is drawn in stall 1 and will be ideally positioned to slot in behind the two front-runners; if he gets a clean passage and the gallop is honest, he is the most dangerous threat to Trojan Sun and his finishing record demands respect.

Boxing Great has won twice in the last month on good ground and arrives only 8 days after his last run — monitor how he settles in midfield, because if the front-runners set a scorching pace he has the profile to come late and cause an upset.

Simple Star steps up markedly from 9f to 2m2f in trip based on his last run — watch how he travels in the first mile, as a horse out of its comfort zone on distance can unsettle the rhythm of those around it before fading.

races.name: Lothian Supply Company Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Wrestling Revenue
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 93 days off, Ben Haslam stable in modest recent form (T14: 3/17); has not won or placed on this specific going combination in five attempts and is likely to struggle getting competitive from the back here.

runners_data.name: Falcon Queen
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent type racing for Mike Smith (T14: 0/9 — no recent winners); has placed fourth once in five good-ground tries without winning, and draw 12 places her wide in a sprint where early position matters.

runners_data.name: Supremissy
runners_data.note: Midfield runner for Iain Jardine with a win and two places on Good in last four outings — the most relevant form line in this field; Greg Fairley knows this horse well and the 16-day break looks ideal, making this the standout profile for the likely race shape.

runners_data.name: Doralee
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with excellent recent handicap form — one win and five places in last fifteen good-ground efforts — and David Nolan's experience from draw 3 gives her a strong chance of getting a clean, close-up passage throughout.

runners_data.name: With Glory
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.94) signals she is effectively racing outside her optimal comfort zone in this crowded pace scenario; 105 days off adds a fitness query, and while she will likely lead, sustaining that lead against this volume of chasers is the concern.

runners_data.name: So Grateful
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old midfield type in excellent current form — three places from seven good-ground runs this season including back-to-back seconds; Billy Garritty rides and the horse's relaxed style suits a scenario where the pace is honest but not chaotic.

runners_data.name: Gwen Tennyson
runners_data.note: Hold-up juvenile for Gemma Tutty with Jake Dickson claiming 5lb; has placed in three of eleven good-ground runs without winning but drew a useful wide draw (13) that can allow her to swing round late if the race develops her way.

runners_data.name: Ski Angel
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse in reality — redistributed forward on the map only because rear slots are overcrowded — so discount the mapped position; six-year-old with headgear (p) and a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting the forced prominent role weakens her realistic chance materially.

runners_data.name: Sixcor
runners_data.note: Prominent type with headgear (p), one win on Good and three places for Linda Perratt; draw 11 is workable and he brings solid recent handicap form, though ten good-ground runs without a recent win from this mark tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Moretons
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old with headgear (b) returning after 82 days off for Simon Waugh (T14: 0/2); form figures show no win or place in eleven good-ground runs and the layoff adds uncertainty, placing this horse at the bottom of the hold-up division's appeal.

runners_data.name: Fear And Fast
runners_data.note: Prominent type for Jim Goldie with Sam James; has posted six consecutive sixth-or-worse finishes on Good and the 58-day break gives little cause to expect a reversal — the form simply has not been there when conditions suit.

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: Hold-up five-year-old rated 49, fitted with headgear (tp) and returning just three days after his last run — very quick turnaround for Mike Smith; won once and placed twice in fifteen good-ground starts and the Strand Scorecard marks him as the top selection at low confidence, which is consistent with his modest but present form claims.

runners_data.name: Hard Nut
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old natural prominent runner for Linda Perratt who is redistributed to midfield on the map because the prominent positions are genuinely full; STYLE_FIT (0.91) and the fade-in-finish flag combine to limit his realistic impact, and at OR 41 off 74 days, form has been consistently modest.

races.paceDynamic: With Glory is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to press from the outside, she should control the tempo from draw 8 on Good ground over this straight 5f at Musselburgh. However, the field is unusually packed with prominent types — Doralee, Falcon Queen, Sixcor, and Fear And Fast all want to race close to the pace — meaning With Glory will not enjoy a completely uncontested lead and the early fractions are unlikely to be truly slow. Hard Nut is a natural front-runner but is redistributed to midfield because the prominent berths are already oversubscribed, so its influence at the head of affairs is unlikely; similarly, Ski Angel, a true hold-up type, is mapped forward only because the rear positions are crowded with horses pushed back from their natural spots. The resulting shape — a competitive but not frantic gallop set by With Glory, with a wall of prominent types tracking — is most likely to suit horses with a strong finishing kick who can settle just off that pace group and emerge in the final furlong, pointing directly towards prominent-to-midfield closers who travel within themselves and power through.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Lead, Strong Finishers
scenarios.trigger: If With Glory controls a fair but sustainable pace and the prominent pack races evenly without burning each other out, midfield runners with genuine finishing speed emerge late.
scenarios.body: With Glory sets an honest but unforced tempo, the prominent cluster of Doralee, Sixcor and Falcon Queen track in a bunch without dramatic scrimmaging, and the race opens up for those with a turn of foot in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pile-Up, Pace Heats Up
scenarios.trigger: If the density of prominent runners creates genuine early pressure on With Glory and the gallop quickens materially, those who drop in mid-pack and produce a sustained late run will gain ground fastest.
scenarios.body: The contest runs hot in the first two furlongs as Doralee, Sixcor and Falcon Queen all compete for position behind With Glory, and the pace bleeds out those who raced prominently, leaving a fresher finisher to pounce.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If With Glory finds an untroubled lead, the pace proves deceptively moderate, and no prominent rival can sustain a serious challenge in the straight.
scenarios.body: With Glory dictates exactly as she pleases with the field fanning out behind but unable to close the gap quickly enough on the Good turf, and a prominent horse benefits by tracking in her slipstream throughout.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos At Front, Rear Comes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners badly interfere with each other early, creating a messy scramble, genuine hold-up horses get a clear run and pick up the pieces late.
scenarios.body: Congestion in the first furlong disrupts the expected order and the hold-up horses — those genuinely at the rear, not the redistributed types — find daylight approaching the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: With Glory (draw 8) will attempt to lead but Doralee (draw 3) and Sixcor (draw 11) are both prominent types who may push across to challenge early — watch whether With Glory actually secures a clear lead or becomes embroiled in a pace battle within the first furlong.

Hard Nut (draw 1) is a natural front-runner squeezed into a midfield role by pace congestion — if Alex Jary (3lb claim) attempts to push forward from the inside rail anyway, a messy scrimmage at the break becomes possible and could unsettle several runners.

Royal Duke ran just three days ago — an unusually quick turnaround — and while Mike Smith has clearly targeted this race, monitor any market move; a horse returned at this short interval sometimes shows a bounce effect, particularly a hold-up type needing peak freshness.

So Grateful has placed in three of her last four starts including two consecutive seconds — if she gets a smooth passage in midfield, Billy Garritty can produce her at exactly the right moment in the straight, and good ground consistently brings out her best.

Supremissy's last-five form on Good (1-3-4-7 in that going band) is the most consistent recent pattern of any runner — watch her price in the market as a genuine guide to whether punters have picked up on the same angle the pace map supports.
